                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Lead and coordinate external design partners across all disciplines, setting clear scopes, deliverables and accountabilities and managing performance against agreed quality, programme and budget expectations.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Manage the application of Volta\u2019s Reference Design and engineering standards to each project, coordinating site-specific adaptations and securing approval from the relevant technical authorities for departures.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Lead multidisciplinary design coordination reviews, resolving interfaces between civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, controls and GPU compute infrastructure to ensure the overall design works as one integrated AI factory.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Act as the principal point of coordination for project design matters, working closely with customers and internal stakeholders to resolve requirements, secure timely decisions and maintain alignment as the design develops.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Plan and lead design reviews and stage gates, ensuring deliverables are complete, coordinated and appropriately reviewed, with comments, actions and approvals tracked to closure.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Work with the Project Controls, Delivery and Procurement teams to define design package boundaries and release priorities, support technical tender evaluations and incorporate supplier and contractor design information into the coordinated project design.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Embed construction sequencing, prefabrication, modular delivery, access, logistics and maintainability into the design, working with the teams that will build and operate the facility.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Manage design changes through a clear change control process, assessing their impact on scope, cost, programme, capacity and performance and securing the required approvals before implementation.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Remain closely engaged during construction, coordinating responses to technical queries, design clarifications, submittals and proposed changes with designers and engineering, so site teams receive timely, approved information.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Work with Operations and commissioning teams to incorporate testing, commissioning, maintenance and handover requirements into the design, including the information needed for safe and effective operation.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Champion best practice health and safety throughout design delivery, leading multidisciplinary reviews to eliminate foreseeable hazards and reduce H&S risks through design.<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              \u203a Maintain clear visibility of design risks, assumptions, interfaces and outstanding decisions, escalating issues early and reporting design delivery status to project leadership<\/p>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                About Tritium Fuel Cycle (TFC)<\/strong>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                GFG is designing a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) fusion power plant (FPP) to deliver 1 GW of electrical power in the 2040s. The \u201cGIGA\u201d plant will be based on a stellarator magnetic confinement fusion device, operating continuously on a deuterium-tritium (D-T) fuel cycle. \u00a0Prior to this, the smaller \u201cGauss Industrial Demonstrator (GID-170)\u201d will be deployed in the mid-2030s.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                While deuterium can be extracted from seawater, tritium is a tightly controlled radioactive isotope with an extremely limited global supply. Therefore, both GID-170 and GIGA must utilise closed tritium fuel cycle infrastructure, to ensure that unburnt tritium is fully recycled back to the stellarator and not released to the environment. Meanwhile, the tritium consumed by the fusion reaction must be replenished using tritium breeding blankets (TBB).

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A first-of-a-kind dedicated tritium fuel cycle (TFC) facility, suitable for continuously supporting a stellarator device, must be designed, built and commissioned. It will adopt a multi-loop process architecture, each loop comprising many deeply integrated subsystems. Developing such a facility presents unique engineering challenges: the supply chain is still emerging, commercial process simulation tools lack dedicated TFC libraries, suitable off-the-shelf equipment is not always available, and some technologies have relatively low technology readiness levels (TRLs).\u00a0

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                A conceptual design is currently under development, with the project then progressing into pre-front-end engineering design (pre-FEED) in 2028, followed by front-end engineering design (FEED) and design for manufacturing phases. Completion of the overall design phase (for GID-170) must be achieved by 2032.<\/span>
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                <\/p>
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                About the role<\/strong>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                GFG is looking for several Tritium Process Engineers to join the TFC department and develop the GID-170 and GIGA TFC facilities. The roles will contribute to the continued development and optimisation of the overall fuel cycle architecture and its subsystems. Activities will include managing design requirements; developing process flow diagrams (PFDs), piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), heat and mass balances (HMBs) and the Basis of Design (BoD); selecting technologies; sizing and arranging equipment; and contributing to safety-related design. The roles may also involve supporting equipment prototype development and testing with technology developers and research partners.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                We welcome candidates with complementary strengths in process design and process modelling and simulation, with systems engineering experience also desirable. These specialisations sit within the same engineering function, and candidates are not expected to have equal expertise across all areas. The number of appointments and balance of responsibilities will reflect the successful candidates\u2019 experience and technical strengths. Drawing on their specialist expertise, successful candidates will work collaboratively on design development, modelling, analysis and optimisation to assess design alternatives and inform robust, well-documented design decisions.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                The TFC comprises a wide range of technologies and subsystems, requiring the department to manage multiple sub-projects and work packages in parallel. Each engineer will contribute across several activities and will be expected to take ownership of specific tasks or subsystems, or lead work packages, depending on their experience. The roles will involve close collaboration with engineers from the same and other disciplines at national and international partner organisations, research institutions and suppliers, as well as with colleagues across disciplines and departments within GFG. Given the specific challenges associated with tritium, close collaboration with Nuclear Safety and Export Control specialists will also be essential.
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                During conceptual design, successful candidates will work closely with the Head of Tritium Fuel Cycle to address the strong interdependencies between subsystems and develop a coherent, integrated design. As the project moves into pre-FEED, they will be expected to take greater day-to-day ownership of their assigned areas and drive design development through pre-FEED and FEED, while maintaining close coordination across subsystem interfaces. As the project progresses, the roles will evolve to support design for manufacture, procurement and commissioning of the GID-170 TFC systems, followed by further development and refinement of the TFC design for GIGA.<\/p>

The next is a world model across every site that predicts the next state in latent space, starting from open world-model weights and growing on field data nobody else holds.<\/p>

That record is your dataset. You will work alongside our perception and model engineers, and your results go into production, not only into papers.<\/p>

About the Role:<\/strong>
You\u2019ll build the operating engine that helps our team turn global campaigns into regional pipeline for EMEA and LATAM. This is a hands-on role. Roughly half your time goes to running regional activation and operations well. The other half goes to automating, templating, and improving that work as a core part of how the team operates. You will work closely with the Global Integrated Campaigns team, Field Marketing, Marketing Ops, EMEA\/LATAM sales leadership, ADRs, Product Marketing & Partner Marketing.<\/p>

<\/p>

Regional activation and localization<\/h3>

  • Help activate ADRs and Sales on localized campaigns.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

    • Lead end-to-end local delivery across digital, email, social and ABM and collaborate with Field marketing on relevant industry events that are part of the overall campaigns. Manage timelines, vendors, and multi-channel coordination to hit regional pipeline targets.<\/p><\/li>

    • Build and launch campaigns and events hands-on in HubSpot (emails, landing pages, forms, lists, workflows) and Salesforce (campaign build-out, list pulls, segmentation), to Marketing Ops standards. Act as Marketing Ops' primary liaison for regional field marketing.<\/p><\/li>

    • Explore new vendors on behalf of the team and take them through Procurement.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

      Operating model and request intake<\/h3>

      • Run the EMEA field marketing request intake: triage against priority tiers and SLAs, and route or decline work that doesn't fit the plan. Partner with marketing operations on behalf of field marketing to leverage use of AI automation.<\/p><\/li>

      • Design and maintain the localization workflow: translation tooling, a brand and terminology glossary, review routing, and vendor management.<\/p><\/li>

      • Translate global campaign strategy into modular playbooks and campaign kits that each region can adapt without rebuilding from scratch<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

        Budget, performance, and insight<\/h3>

        • Manage and forecast the regional campaign budget, and allocate it across channels and programs for maximum ROI.<\/p><\/li>

        • Define regional KPIs (MQLs, cost per MQL, pipeline influence, revenue impact). Own reporting and attribution hygiene across regions, including data quality in Salesforce and HubSpot.<\/p><\/li>

        • Measure the operational impact of your work: hours returned to the team, request cycle time, and campaign activation speed.<\/p><\/li>

        • Bring local market feedback on competitors, customer needs, and emerging opportunities to Product Marketing, Global Campaigns, and leadership.<\/p><\/li>

        • Partner with the Senior Field Marketing Managers to align the operating model with pipeline goals.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

          What you bring:<\/strong><\/p>

          • Ability and\/or willingness to use\u00a0our product<\/a>.<\/p><\/li>

          • 7+ years in B2B marketing, field marketing, or program operations, ideally in B2B software. You have a record of running integrated, pipeline-focused programs.<\/p><\/li>

          • Hands-on experience as a Senior Field Marketing Manager (or equivalent regional field marketing role) running events, account-based campaigns, and sales partnership.<\/p><\/li>

          • Strong hands-on skills in Salesforce and HubSpot (or a comparable CRM and marketing automation platform), including building campaigns and reporting on performance.<\/p><\/li>

          • Demonstrated experience building automations with workflow tools such as Claude and Zapier, or with scripting that connects systems. You know how to apply LLM tools to real operational work and where human review is required.<\/p><\/li>

          • Experience running multi-region programs, with an understanding of how regions and languages differ operationally.<\/p><\/li>

          • Strong program management: organized, detail-oriented, and comfortable juggling many programs, vendors, and stakeholders at once.<\/p><\/li>

          • A process-oriented, analytical mindset. You document what you build, measure what it does, and use data (A\/B testing, attribution) to improve it.<\/p><\/li>

          • Excellent written and verbal English. You can influence sales leaders, AEs, and senior marketers, and present to executives.<\/p><\/li>

          • You are self-motivated, outcome-focused, and comfortable in a fast-paced, ambiguous environment.<\/p><\/li>

          • Experience supporting field marketing or sales organizations in EMEA (LATAM a plus).<\/p><\/li>

          • Experience managing budgets over \u20ac500K.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

            Nice-to-haves:<\/strong><\/p>

            • Experience with localization or translation management tools, or working with translation vendors.<\/p><\/li>

            • Fluency in a second European or Latin American language.<\/p><\/li>

            • Familiarity with ABM strategies and tools, and with event platforms and attendee data flows.<\/p><\/li>

            • Experience marketing to enterprise or technical buyers (developers, architects, platform teams), or a background in automation, orchestration, or workflow software.<\/p><\/li>

            • Experience mentoring a team.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

You own a documented automation roadmap across EMEA and LATAM, and regional campaigns show a clear link to pipeline.<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

                      About Odys<\/strong><\/h2>

                      At Odys, we\u2019re mobilizing power, with Hybrid Power Systems developed for aerospace and in-demand everywhere. It\u2019s the kind of mission diversity that demands a fresh way of thinking.<\/p>

                      We began with an early bet on hybrid, when the mobility industry was focused on batteries. We designed, tested, and validated our first 1 MW high-speed generator in 12 months. And then we pushed further, developing systems with greater power density in less time. Today, our Hybrid Power Systems offer outputs ranging from 20 kW<\/strong> to 4 MW<\/strong>, with applications in the air or on the ground.<\/p>

                      One of those applications is Laila<\/strong>, an unmanned drone designed for critical logistics and defense missions. With its 100 kW-class onboard Hybrid Power System, Laila can support medical cold-chain transport or serve as an aerial platform for counter-UAS measures.<\/p>

                      The market interest has been overwhelming: Over 30<\/strong> inbound requests from leading US and global manufacturers, and 14+ DoD<\/strong> contracts<\/strong>.<\/p>

                      Our team comes from deep tech and aerospace, with backgrounds spanning drone and aircraft development, high-volume production, and electrified mobility.<\/p>

                      We operate with urgency and ownership at every level. We validated high-speed generator technology faster than our peers, not because we skipped steps, but because we've been doing this long enough to know which ones matter most.<\/p>

                      Creating the future<\/strong> of power, in the air and on the ground, is a challenge we\u2019ve been training our entire lives for. If that sounds like you, this is the opportunity you\u2019ve been waiting for.<\/p>

                      \u00a0<\/div>

                      About The Role<\/strong><\/h1>

                      Odys Aviation is seeking a senior airworthiness lead for our UAS portfolio, starting with Laila, our hybrid-electric VTOL UAS for logistics and defense missions. The role sits with Odys Aviation GmbH in Munich, our European entity, and works daily with our engineering and test teams in the US.<\/p>

                      The path is set: SORA SAIL III, then SAIL IV with an EASA DVR under SC Light-UAS, then DOA under Part 21 Subpart J and RTC or TC for larger products. EASA is our lead authority. The FAA is equally in scope, and our customers bring authorities from Europe, the Middle East, and APAC to the table.<\/p>

                      This is a builder role. There is no legacy DOA to inherit and no large compliance department to delegate to. You set up design assurance in a way that fits a fast-moving hardware team, verify evidence yourself, and stay close to the aircraft through lab, ground, and flight testing.<\/p>

                      You bridge two cultures: US engineering speed and European certification rigor. You know where the rules are still being written, and you help write them. Your credibility with authorities is an asset for the company, and your judgment on where effort pays off is an asset for the team. <\/p>

                      Don't meet all desired requirements?<\/strong> Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Odys, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway.<\/p>

                      <\/p>

                      What You'll Do<\/strong><\/h2>

                      • Own SORA compliance strategy and evidence for SAIL III and SAIL IV, including the EASA DVR from application to closure<\/p><\/li>

                      • Obtain operational authorizations across jurisdictions from one evidence base<\/p><\/li>

                      • Drive design assurance across the group and perform compliance verification of engineering evidence reports<\/p><\/li>

                      • Build DOA readiness for higher SAIL, RTC, and TC<\/p><\/li>

                      • Set the regulatory frame for each test campaign and turn compliance needs into lab, ground, and flight test objectives that earn compliance credit<\/p><\/li>

                      • Ensure flight test safety reviews are timely and run with certification rigor; back up the Safety Lead<\/p><\/li>

                      • Represent Odys in EASA and FAA rulemaking, JARUS, EUROCAE, ASTM, SAE, RTCA, and GAMA<\/p><\/li>

                      • Be the internal reference on what compliance requires, and on what it does not<\/p><\/li><\/ul>

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Your tasks<\/h2>\n

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Imagine fleets of autonomous forklifts, each weighing several tons, lifting heavy loads into racks up to 14 meters high, safely and around the clock, right next to people. That's what we build at Jungheinrich Robotics, and AI-assisted engineering plays an important role in how we do it. In this role, you help ensure that every one of these vehicles moves exactly as intended. <\/p>\n

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              We are hiring at both Senior and Staff levels. Apply for the role that fits you best, and we'll find the right fit together! <\/p>\n

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                \n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • You develop and take ownership of control software components for our autonomous forklifts, from the hardware abstraction layer and actuator control based on ros_control\/ros2_control to the interfaces with localization and navigation.<\/li>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • You model and implement vehicle kinematics for different forklift types, including acceleration- and jerk-limited motion.<\/li>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • You integrate motor controllers, drives, and actuators using fieldbus systems, particularly CANopen.<\/li>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • You integrate and calibrate robot sensors, including encoders, IMUs, laser scanners, cameras, and lift height sensors.<\/li>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • You improve the reliability of our robots in real-world environments through intelligent error handling, automated recovery mechanisms, and logging and analysis tools.<\/li>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • You define and execute integration and system-level tests on real robots, test benches, and in simulation.<\/li>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • You use AI-assisted engineering tools in your daily work, from coding and test generation to log analysis.<\/li>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              • You contribute to technical concepts and the development of our control architecture while supporting less experienced colleagues.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Requirements<\/h2>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  \n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • You hold a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, or bring equivalent practical experience.<\/li>\n
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                • You bring at least 4 years of professional experience in robotics software development, including at least 2 years working with real mobile robots.<\/li>\n

Take-home assignment (Step 1 of the process)

Please complete a take-home assignment. You are allowed to use LLMs to write code. To ensure that your work will not be used at Fluence, we’ve made it unrelated to healthcare:

Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows

A simple app where neighbors list tools they are willing to lend, request to borrow from each other, and receive automated notifications and reminders handled by n8n.

Stack

  • Next.js (App Router)

  • Clerk for authentication

  • Convex for data + backend logic

Requirements

Public page

  • The fictional company name is LendLoop.

  • Short tagline, e.g. “Borrow what you need. Lend what you don’t.”

  • Show:

  • A read-only list of available tools (name and category only, no owner details), pulled from Convex.

Authenticated experience

  • Keep secrets in environment variables and n8n credentials, never in code or exported workflow JSON.

Description

We’re growing and looking to hire a Learning Experience Designer who embodies our core values: People First, Customer Obsession, Strive for Excellence, and Integrity.

Claroty is a global leader in protecting cyber-physical systems (CPS), dedicated to securing the critical infrastructure that keeps the world running. We’re a fast-growing, award-winning team where innovation meets purpose, and we want you to help us define the future of cybersecurity.

About the Role

As the Learning Experience Designer (GTM Enablement) at Claroty, you will own the design and development of high-impact learning experiences that strengthen go-to-market execution across our Sales and Sales Engineering organizations: eLearning development, instructor-led training, multimedia learning, and platform management.

Reporting to the Sr. Manager, GTM Enablement, this role will focus primarily on developing scalable learning programs for Claromates, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to effectively position, pitch, and demonstrate Claroty's solutions.

You will also develop foundational learning content covering Claroty's markets, products, solutions, buyer personas, and value propositions. This content will serve as a shared foundation for enablement programs across internal teams, customers, and our global Partner community.

Working closely with Sales, Sales Engineering, Product Marketing, and subject matter experts, you will translate complex technical concepts and real-world field expertise into engaging, structured, and reusable learning experiences delivered through live instruction, eLearning, video, and other digital formats.

Responsibilities

As a Learning Experience Designer, your impact will be:

  • ﻿Design and develop GTM learning experiences for internal audiences focused on discovery, positioning, pitching, and demo execution
  • End-to-end project ownership over development processes for GTM enablement initiatives.
  • Create foundational content covering Claroty's markets, products, solutions, buyer personas, and value propositions for reuse across all audiences
  • Produce engaging multimedia learning assets, including eLearning, microlearning videos, interactive modules, and supporting collateral
  • Develop instructor-led (ILT), virtual instructor-led (vILT), webinar, and train-the-trainer programs that enable scalable, expert-led instruction
  • Design and maintain L100 Foundations and L200 Navigation coursework aligned to Claroty's global proficiency framework
  • Partner with Sales, Sales Engineering, Product Marketing, and other subject matter experts to translate field expertise into effective learning experiences
  • Build modular, reusable learning assets and structured learning paths across LMS, CMS, and Partner platforms
  • Continuously improve content quality and effectiveness through learner feedback, consumption metrics, and GTM performance insights

Requirements

What you need to succeed in this role:

  • 3-5 years of experience in instructional design, learning experience design, sales enablement, technical enablement, or a related discipline
  • Demonstrated experience designing and developing learning programs for Sales, Sales Engineering, or other go-to-market audiences
  • Strong understanding of adult learning principles, instructional design methodologies, and competency-based learning
  • Experience developing eLearning, microlearning, interactive learning modules, and multimedia instructional content
  • Proficiency with learning authoring tools such as Articulate 360, Easygenerator, Adobe Creative Cloud, or similar platforms
  • Experience designing instructor-led, virtual instructor-led, webinar, and blended learning programs
  • Ability to translate complex technical concepts, product capabilities, and business value propositions into clear, engaging learning experiences
  • Familiarity with enterprise LMS and CMS platforms, including publishing, organizing, and maintaining digital learning content
  • Strong visual communication and content production skills, including presentation design, video production, and learning asset development
  • Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple content development initiatives and competing priorities
  • Excellent communication, collaboration, and stakeholder management skills

About Claroty

Claroty empowers organizations to protect the mission-critical infrastructure that underpins modern life. The AI-powered Claroty Platform serves as the single source of operational truth, providing the deepest visibility and broadest protection across cyber-physical systems (CPS), leveraging five core solutions: asset inventory, exposure management, network protection, secure access, and threat detection. Claroty helps organizations operationalize CPS protection through a programmatic approach designed to reduce risk, maintain operational integrity, and meet compliance–whether in the cloud with Claroty xDome or on-premise with Claroty Continuous Threat Detection (CTD). Claroty is deployed by hundreds of organizations at thousands of sites globally. The company is headquartered in New York City and has a presence in Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. To learn more, visit.

A Great Place to Work® certified company, Claroty is headquartered in New York City with employees across the world. The company is widely recognized as the industry leader in CPS protection, with backing from the world’s largest investment firms and industrial automation vendors, named a Leader in The Forrester Wave™: IoT Security Solutions, Q3 2025, recognized by KLAS Research as Best in KLAS for Healthcare IoT Security five years in a row, and ranking on the Forbes Cloud 100 and Deloitte Technology Fast 500 for multiple consecutive years.

Expected compensation for the role is between $110,000 - $125,000. This is a good faith estimate but does not include equity, bonus, or other forms of payment. Pay will be determined by experience level, but those outside the salary band are welcome to apply.

Claroty is an equal-opportunity employer committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment for all. We encourage applications from candidates of ALL diverse backgrounds, and special accommodations are available upon request in all selection phases.

Medical Virtual Assistant (MVA)

Remote | Chiropractic Clinic | 30 Hours/Week | $5-$6.50/hour
performance-based increase after 6 months

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly capable Medical Virtual Assistant (MVA) to support the overall operational health of a busy healthcare clinic. This role is ideal for someone who is very sharp, proactive, detail-oriented, emotionally intelligent, and able to take ownership of important clinic workflows with minimal supervision.

This is not a basic task-following role. The ideal candidate must be able to think ahead, identify operational gaps, take initiative, and help remove administrative and billing-related tasks from the provider's plate.

We are looking for someone with excellent English communication skills, strong executive presence, high accountability, and the ability to build a trust-based working relationship with the provider and care team.

Key Responsibilities

Insurance Verification

Verify patient insurance after the patient checks in, typically around 15 minutes after the scheduled appointment time. Ensure all insurance information is accurate, updated, and properly documented.

Denied Claims Management

Review denied claims, identify denial reasons, and assist with claim reprocessing. Track issues, follow up on missing information, and help prevent repeat claim errors.

EOB Processing

Review and process Explanation of Benefits documents. Help organize, validate, and clear EOB backlogs while ensuring billing and insurance documentation is accurate.

Patient Balance Resolution

Review outstanding insurance balances and patient account issues. Track unresolved balances, identify the source of the issue, and coordinate next steps for resolution.

Claims Processing

Support claims-related workflows, including Cigna and Veterans Affairs claims. Ensure claims are reviewed, tracked, and escalated when necessary.

Payment Coordination

Assist with vendor payment coordination, including check payments when needed. Ensure payment-related tasks are completed accurately and on time.

SOAP Note Monitoring

Monitor SOAP note completion, accuracy, and compliance. Track missing, incomplete, or delayed documentation and communicate concerns appropriately.

Appointment Tracking

Track missed appointments, canceled appointments, and scheduling trends. Identify patterns that may affect clinic revenue, patient flow, or provider productivity.

Reports and Operational Tracking

Prepare reports on outstanding balances, missed appointments, canceled appointments, EOB backlog, denied claims, and other operational metrics. Reports should include clear insights and practical recommendations when needed.

Team Coordination

Support smooth communication between the provider, care team, and administrative staff. Help ensure updates are clearly shared, priorities are followed through, and important tasks are not missed.

Operational Support

Proactively identify workflow gaps, billing concerns, documentation delays, scheduling issues, and patient account problems. Recommend practical solutions to improve clinic efficiency.

Mandatory Requirements

  • Minimum of 1 year of experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant

  • Experience supporting a US healthcare practice

  • Experience with insurance verification, EOBs, claims, denied claims, patient balances, or billing support

  • Exposure to CPT and ICD-10 codes

  • Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal

  • Strong executive presence and professional communication style

  • Must be a Mac OS user

  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through

  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

  • Proven leadership, ownership, or high-accountability experience in a previous role

Required Soft Skills

  • Proactive and able to anticipate needs before being asked

  • Highly detail-oriented with billing, documentation, and reporting tasks

  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills

  • Emotionally intelligent and patient when working with a busy provider

  • Confident, professional, and organized in communication

  • Able to take personal responsibility for assigned work

  • Resourceful and self-motivated when learning new workflows

  • Trustworthy, dependable, and comfortable handling sensitive information

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience supporting a chiropractic clinic

  • Experience with Cigna or Veterans Affairs claims

  • Experience clearing EOB or billing backlogs

  • Experience preparing operational or billing reports

  • Experience mentoring, training, or supporting new team members

  • Experience working closely with a clinic owner, provider, or executive-level leader

Schedule and Compensation

  • Schedule: Monday to Friday

  • Hours: 6 hours per day, 30 hours per week

  • Rate: $6 per hour

  • Work Setup: Remote

  • Device Requirement: Mac OS required

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is someone who does not wait to be told every step. This person should be observant, organized, and confident enough to identify what needs attention.

They should be able to manage detailed billing and administrative tasks while also thinking about the bigger picture of clinic operations. The right candidate will be sharp, emotionally intelligent, highly reliable, and capable of becoming a trusted operational support partner for the provider and care team.

MDM Subject Matter Expert | About You

As an MDM Subject Matter Expert, you will provide senior design assurance and specialized guidance across enterprise identity resolution, golden-record design, matching, survivorship, stewardship, and data governance. You will work alongside architects, technical leads, developers, and business stakeholders to validate critical design decisions, review milestone deliverables, and resolve complex data and mastering issues. You bring extensive practical knowledge from real-world MDM implementations and can balance technical design, business ownership, stewardship usability, governance, and long-term operating sustainability.

MDM Subject Matter Expert | Day-to-Day

  • Provide senior oversight and design assurance for MDM architecture, entity models, identity-resolution strategies, golden records, hierarchies, relationships, and stewardship processes.
  • Review and validate matching, duplicate identification, confidence scoring, survivorship, source precedence, merge/unmerge, and exception-management rules.
  • Advise business owners and data stewards on critical data elements, ownership models, governance decision rights, stewardship thresholds, and exception-resolution processes.
  • Conduct milestone reviews to verify that solution designs, configurations, pipelines, data-quality controls, and deployment deliverables meet approved requirements and MDM best practices.
  • Support the resolution of complex matching, data-quality, lineage, persistent-identifier, scalability, and stewardship issues encountered during design, build, testing, or deployment.
  • Review commercial-platform and custom-build approaches, highlighting long-term considerations related to total cost of ownership, licensing, customization, upgrades, and internal support capacity.
  • Guide teams on explainable and reversible mastering practices, ensuring that match and survivorship decisions are traceable to source records and supported by complete audit history.
  • Contribute to knowledge-transfer materials, rule catalogs, stewardship procedures, and operating-model documentation that enable sustainable business ownership.

MDM Subject Matter Expert | Skills & Experience

  • 12+ years of experience in Master Data Management, Data Governance, Data Quality, or Enterprise Information Management, including senior advisory or design-assurance responsibilities.
  • Deep expertise in entity resolution, deterministic and probabilistic matching, survivorship, hierarchy management, crosswalks, golden records, stewardship, and exception management.
  • Experience with MDM platforms such as Profisee, Informatica MDM, Reltio, Ataccama, Stibo Systems, or comparable commercial solutions.
  • Strong understanding of customer, constituent, supporter, provider, supplier, product, or similar master-data domains and the challenges associated with cross-system identity resolution.
  • Experience reviewing MDM architecture, configuration, data quality, governance, testing, and operational-readiness deliverables across complex implementations.
  • Strong advisory and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence business and technical teams, challenge design assumptions, and resolve complex MDM decisions.

Engagement details

Role Title: Program Analyst, Federal Agency Experience

Role type: Contractor

Location: Remote, US-based only

Commitment: 12-15 hours per week, flexible around your schedule, part-time, project-based

Compensation: $60 - $80USD per hour

About the opportunity

This role is for people who have worked as program or management analysts for a federal agency (GS-0343, GS-0301, or equivalent), or supported one as a contractor, and are based in the US. If that's not you, this one isn't a fit.

micro1 is seeking Program Analyst, Federal Agency Experience for a customer project focused on AI evaluation. You'll write realistic scenarios from federal program and policy work, write the correct answer for each, and review scenarios and answers written by other specialists. Your knowledge of how federal agencies plan, evaluate, and report on programs is what matters. No prior AI experience is required.

What you'll do

  1. Write realistic scenarios based on situations you've handled, such as a program performance review, a decision memo for a senior leader, an executive briefing, or an after-action report.
  2. Write the reference answer for each scenario: what the analyst should recommend or produce, and which policies, guidance, or reporting requirements support it.
  3. Review scenarios and answers written by other specialists. Flag unrealistic assumptions and wrong citations, and explain what should change.
  4. Check that each scenario reflects how federal planning, evaluation, and reporting actually work in an agency.
  5. Work with project coordinators to resolve unclear scenarios or answers.
  6. Use fictional or public information only. Do not include non-public agency documents, pre-decisional material, CUI, or PII.

Required qualifications

  1. Hands-on experience as a federal program or management analyst (GS-0343, GS-0301, or equivalent), including as a contractor supporting a federal agency, in at least one of these areas: program evaluation or performance measurement, policy analysis, strategic or operational planning, decision memos and briefings for senior leaders [confirm].
  2. Working knowledge of how federal agencies plan, measure, and report on programs.
  3. Ability to explain why a recommendation is sound and what tradeoffs it carries.
  4. Based in the United States.

Preferred qualifications

  1. Recent hands-on practice in federal program or policy analysis.
  2. Experience writing program evaluations, after-action reports, or briefings for senior leaders.
  3. Experience supporting headquarters, program offices, or planning staff.
  4. Experience with performance measurement or strategic planning in government.

Current federal employees: please check your agency's outside-employment rules before applying.

Application process

  1. Apply. Submit your application and resume.
  2. Complete the Federal Program Analysis interview. It's a short, spoken interview about real program and policy situations you've handled. Finishing it is what moves your application forward, so please complete it as soon as you can.
  3. Review. We review your interview and background against the project needs.
  4. Onboarding. If selected, you'll receive contract terms and project instructions before you start.

About micro1

micro1 is a data lab that connects professionals with opportunities to apply their expertise to customer projects. We work with specialists across fields such as engineering, finance, healthcare, and law to support AI labs and enterprises. Through our extended network, contributors bring their knowledge and judgment to projects with their own scope, requirements, and engagement terms.

Job Title: QA Engineer for Mobile (Remote)

Job Location: London, United Kingdom

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Veeva Systems is a mission-driven organization and pioneer in industry cloud, helping life sciences companies bring therapies to patients faster. As one of the fastest-growing SaaS companies in history, we surpassed $3B in revenue in our last fiscal year with extensive growth potential ahead.
At the heart of Veeva are our values: Do the Right Thing, Customer Success, Employee Success, and Speed. We're not just any public company – we made history in 2021 by becoming a public benefit corporation (PBC), legally bound to balancing the interests of customers, employees, society, and investors.
As a Work Anywhere company, we support your flexibility to work from home or in the office, so you can thrive in your ideal environment.
Join us in transforming the life sciences industry, committed to making a positive impact on its customers, employees, and communities.

The Role

The Veeva Link mobile team is looking for an experienced QA Engineer to help us ensure the high quality of our iOS App. You will help the mobile team to validate the app releases, find potential issues early and ensure a great customer experience by writing manual and automated tests for native iOS applications (SwiftUI/UIKit). At Veeva Link, we're building the intelligence layer for life sciences, creating connected data applications that accelerate drug development and significantly improve patient outcomes. Our core belief: combining the highest quality data with state-of-the-art software delivers immense value.

We believe execution matters most. Progress comes from speed, accuracy, and quality in what we build every day. Our engineering approach emphasizes clear product definitions leading to meticulous technical designs. We leverage a modern tech stack to deliver inherently reliable applications and a great user experience.

Our work spans two critical areas:

Data-Driven Insights

We develop sophisticated applications that map and understand global scientific and medical expertise, providing high-impact insights and AI-generated intelligence. Engineers here tackle complex data modeling, entity resolution, and advanced machine learning.

Intelligent Business Workflows

We engineer workflow applications powered by our data, using AI to find patterns and route information precisely. This involves designing scalable pipelines and intelligent automation.

Why Join Veeva Link?

Build products that create a significant positive impact in global healthcare.
Work in an environment led by a CEO with an engineering background.
Work Anywhere means you can work in an office or at home on any given day.
Empowered Autonomy: Tech decisions are made within teams, giving engineers significant autonomy.
Collaborate with highly skilled teammates who take pride in achieving great outcomes. Excellence matters.

What You'll Do

    • Partner with mobile engineers to identify, isolate, and troubleshoot complex application defects
    • Scale and optimize the mobile test automation framework and codebase
    • Design and implement comprehensive test plans to validate existing application features
    • Collaborate with software engineers to establish robust testing protocols for new feature development
    • Anticipate complex user scenarios and edge cases to engineer thorough test coverage
    • Document and escalate defects via GitHub issues to deliver actionable insights to the Engineering team

Requirements

    • Quality oriented mindset
    • 4+ years of experience working as a Quality Assurance Engineer for mobile
    • Combination of in-depth knowledge of quality assurance, solid understanding of mobile technologies, as well as knowledge of automation tools
    • Experience in manual testing, including checking network calls using Man-in-the-middle/Proxy (e.g. Charles, ProxyMan)
    • Familiarity with Cloud testing platforms (e.g. SauceLabs, LambdaTest)
    • Proficiency in writing native app code tests (e.g. XCUITest, etc)
    • Experience with Command line tools for iOS (xcrun, xcode-select, xcodebuild, npm, etc), as well as with configuration management or version control tools (e.g. git)
    • Proactively make continuous improvements regarding test coverage, execution and automation.
    • Experience with continuous integration software (e.g. GitHub Actions, Jenkins, TrevisCI, etc).
    • Good communication and interpersonal skills
    • Excellent command of the English language
    • Passion for all things mobile
    • AI-forward mindset: comfortable leveraging AI tools to speed up test case design, automation scripting, and debugging

Nice to Have

    • DevOps
    • Experience in writing workflows for GitHub Actions

Perks & Benefits

    • Pension scheme
    • Life Assurance/Death Benefits
    • Paid Maternity & Paternity Leave
    • International Travel Insurance
    • Cigna Travel Insurance
    • Optum Global Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
    • Veeva 1% Giving (charity contribution)
    • Fitness reimbursements
    • Home internet connection reimbursement
