    We’re looking for a Senior C++/iOS Engineer to join the Baldur squad within User Platform (UP). Baldur owns Spotify’s Session Management and Delegated Authorization domains—the systems that enable applications to securely obtain, use, and manage access tokens for hundreds of millions of users. In this role, you’ll help shape the technology that powers secure access across every Spotify client and third-party integration. 

    Your work will support engineers across Spotify building mobile and desktop experiences, platform teams, and third-party developers integrating with Spotify’s authorization platform. You’ll collaborate across disciplines to build secure, reliable, and scalable authentication experiences that have a direct impact on millions of people every day.

  • Design, build, and evolve critical infrastructure powering Spotify applications and partner integrations using shared C++ libraries and native Swift on iOS.
  • Develop secure, reliable, and performant delegated authorization flows, including token issuance, refresh, revocation, and session lifecycle management across multiple platforms.
  • Partner with client and backend engineers to integrate with core authorization services, token issuance, client registration, and token revocation.
  • Improve how credentials and access tokens are securely stored and managed on-device while balancing security, reliability, and application performance.
  • Contribute to the evolution of Spotify’s authorization frameworks, Spotify-specific implementations, enabling new platforms and product experiences.
  • Drive technical improvements, share knowledge with teammates, and help shape the long-term technical direction of delegated authorization and session management.

    The Music Mission team owns Spotify's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.

    We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join the Artist-First AI Music lab. Our team explores and advances generative technologies for music to create new experiences for fans and artists, with a focus on listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles:

    Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We'll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later.

    Choice in participation: We recognize there's a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music.

    Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions.

    Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will use our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections.

    For more information, see this press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/

    ","id":"babebec3-0061-4c39-a4ad-c51a54d23567","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Lead foundational measurement and insights work for generative music experiences, developing the frameworks that help Spotify understand how creators, listeners, and rights holders engage with generative AI music.
  • Design and run large-scale analyses and evaluations of generative music systems, from prompt interpretation to model output quality, using Spotify's unique behavioral datasets, annotations, and experimentation platforms.
  • Partner with Engineers and AI Researchers to integrate evaluation signals into model development loops, debugging workflows, and product iteration, making sure scientific rigor informs technical direction.
  • Identify the behavioral and market dynamics that shape sustainable consumer demand and creator participation, and translate them into clear strategic recommendations.
  • Build practical, scalable metrics and decision systems that define what "good" looks like for AI music: credibility, user delight, safety, creator alignment, and ecosystem trust.
  • Bring together model, user behavior, and ecosystem signals into clear narratives that shape product strategy, cross-functional alignment, and long-term priorities across Spotify.
  • Create the datasets, dashboards, and long-term measurement systems that give Spotify a lasting, comprehensive understanding of product health and impact.
  • Work closely with Product, Design, Research, Legal, Trust & Safety, Marketing, Policy, and Licensing teams, bringing statistical rigor and principled measurement to help build artist-first systems that scale responsibly.
    • "},{"text":"Who You Are ","content":"
  • You have a track record of using insights to shape strategy for major company initiatives involving many different partners.
  • You have significant hands-on experience in advanced analytics or data science, ideally in a domain involving LLM evaluation, user-generated content, or complex user behavior.
  • You communicate clearly, form well-founded, evidence-backed points of view, and can bring together messy, multimodal signals (quantitative, qualitative, and model telemetry) into clear narratives for senior executives, researchers, engineers, and the music industry.
  • You're proficient in advanced analytics with Python and SQL, have analyzed large datasets, and use AI tools (e.g. Cursor, Copilot) to increase your productivity and impact.
  • You have experience developing metrics frameworks for complex products that help teams measure impact and reason clearly about priorities.
  • You have experience with machine learning frameworks, designing and assessing multimodal or embedding-based models, and validating them against LLM judges or human ground truth, with an understanding of how to evaluate models beyond offline accuracy.
  • You have a solid grounding in experimental design and causal inference, such as A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and power analysis.
  • You thrive when tackling loosely defined problems in ambiguous, zero-to-one spaces.
    • "},{"text":"Where You'll Be ","content":"

  • Manage multiple learning projects from initial scoping through delivery while creating clarity around priorities, timelines, and stakeholder expectations.

    Spotify is shaping the future of advertising by connecting brands with fans through audio, video, and experiences that are part of people's everyday lives. As our advertising business grows, we're focused on bringing innovative products to market, helping advertisers succeed, and turning new ideas into meaningful business growth.

    We're looking for a Senior Director, Global Advertising Product Marketing to lead the next chapter of our global Advertising Product Marketing team. Reporting to the Head of Advertising Business Marketing, you'll work closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, and Marketing leaders to shape product strategy, strengthen our market position, and help advertisers get more value from Spotify.

    This is an opportunity to build and lead a product marketing function with a clear voice in product decisions and a direct impact on business growth. You'll bring customer insights into product development, establish a disciplined approach to go-to-market execution and product adoption, create compelling reasons for advertisers to choose Spotify, and help a global team deliver measurable results.

    ","id":"b9533f31-7bff-43f6-aaf0-60003f017d88","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"
  • Set the vision, strategy, and operating model for global Advertising Product Marketing, connecting advertiser needs, product innovation, competitive insights, and business growth.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, Business Development, and Marketing leaders to bring customer and market insights into product decisions and turn innovation into solutions advertisers value.
  • Lead global go-to-market strategies for Spotify's advertising products, including brand and performance advertising, self-service, programmatic, and emerging solutions. Own product positioning, messaging, packaging, launches, and adoption.
  • Build a deeper understanding of advertisers, agencies, buying behaviors, and the competitive landscape. Use these insights to identify opportunities, influence product priorities, and strengthen Spotify's position in the market.
  • Drive product adoption and commercial growth by identifying customer needs, addressing barriers to adoption, and partnering with teams to improve product usage, retention, and revenue. Define clear measures of success and use results to guide future decisions.
  • Turn complex advertising technology, data, and measurement capabilities into clear, differentiated customer value propositions tied to measurable business outcomes. Partner with Business Marketing to create a consistent story across products and help advertisers understand the impact Spotify can deliver.
  • Strengthen how products move from development to market. Establish clear processes, shared accountability, and measures of readiness that help teams make informed decisions about when to launch, scale, improve, or stop initiatives.
  • Equip Sales and regional teams with the insights, messaging, and tools they need to bring Spotify's advertising solutions to customers. 
  • Work with Measurement and Advertising Effectiveness teams to connect product capabilities with credible evidence of advertiser outcomes, and feed that evidence back into product decisions
  • Explore how AI, automation, and emerging advertising technologies can improve our products, customer experiences, and product marketing practices and identify opportunities to rethink how Spotify develops, positions, and scales its advertising solutions.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing global Product Marketing organization, attracting outstanding talent, strengthening strategic and commercial capabilities, and creating a culture of creativity, accountability, collaboration, and measurable impact.

    The Policy & Safety team sits within Content Platform in the Experience Mission, building the systems that keep Spotify safe, compliant, and trusted by millions of users and creators. This team owns Spotify’s content moderation infrastructure — from detection models to policy enforcement systems and compliance data pipelines.

    Working at the intersection of machine learning, platform engineering, and regulatory compliance, the team partners closely with Trust & Safety, Legal, and Public Affairs. They’re on the critical path for every new content type and social feature — including messaging, comments, and collaborative experiences — ensuring safety is built in from day one.     The Platform team creates the technology that enables Spotify to learn quickly and scale easily, enabling rapid growth in our users and our business around the globe. Spanning many disciplines, we work to make the business work; creating the infrastructure, tooling, frameworks, and capabilities needed to welcome a billion customers.

    Spotify is looking for a Senior Software Engineer to join the Authorization team within Platform. Our team builds and operates the authorization and permissioning systems that enable creators and their teams to securely access and manage their presence across Spotify. What began by supporting Spotify for Artists has grown into foundational capabilities used across Spotify, including Music, Podcasts, and Audiobooks.

    This is a backend-focused role working on systems that sit on a critical path for Spotify's creator ecosystem. You'll help us evolve these systems as they grow in scale and complexity, bringing strong backend engineering expertise while collaborating across product, frontend, and data when needed.

  • Improve the systems and workflows that enable creators to gain access to their content, profiles, and teams.

  • Make thoughtful technical decisions and trade-offs, balancing long-term architecture with solutions that meet current product and business needs.

  • Partner with engineers and cross-functional collaborators across Spotify to understand authorization needs and build reusable platform capabilities.

  • Contribute to frontend experiences and data-related work when useful, while bringing deep expertise and leadership to backend engineering.

  • Raise engineering quality through strong technical judgment, design discussions, operational excellence, and knowledge sharing across the team.

    We design Spotify’s consumer experience—end to end, moment to moment, across every screen, platform, and partner integration. Our mission is to make listening feel effortless, personal, and joyful for billions of users around the world. That means turning complexity into clarity across hundreds of touchpoints—from our mobile and desktop apps to the smart speakers, TVs, cars, and integrations where Spotify shows up every day.     The Content Platform team powers the full lifecycle of content across music, podcasts, audiobooks, and emerging formats at Spotify. We ensure that everything from licensed catalog to user-generated content is understood, trusted, safe, and high quality for millions of listeners worldwide. Our systems are responsible for how content is ingested, understood, enriched, governed, and distributed across the platform.

    As the scale and diversity of content continue to grow—driven by advances in AI, new creation tools, and emerging content formats—we’re investing in intelligent systems that can understand, evaluate, manage, and route content reliably at global scale.

    We’re hiring Senior Staff Machine Learning Engineers to build and scale foundational ML systems that power content understanding, safety, policy enforcement, and decisioning across Spotify. Depending on your experience and interests, you may focus on areas ranging from multimodal content understanding and platform-level ML systems to safety, risk detection, policy enforcement, and compliance.

    You’ll help shape the architecture and technical strategy behind how Spotify understands and makes decisions about content at global scale. This work is foundational to delivering safe, high-quality experiences for listeners and creators while enabling new ways for people to interact with content across Spotify.

    ","id":"47d4eabf-8d5a-4dab-ac72-de7b5b56841c","lists":[{"text":"What You Will Do","content":"
  • Define and drive machine learning strategy across content understanding, safety, policy enforcement, and platform-level decisioning
  • Build and scale production ML systems for classification, moderation, ranking, risk detection, and content evaluation
  • Develop automated decisioning systems that support content quality, integrity, safety, and policy compliance at scale
  • Design and deploy ML systems across multiple content modalities, including text, audio, image, and video
  • Build systems capable of evaluating and making decisions about content in real time and at Spotify scale

  • Build content recommendation systems for emerging agentic and AI-powered user experiences.
  • Train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize large language models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), distillation, and parameter-efficient training approaches.

    The Music Mission team owns Spotify's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale.

    The Artist & Label Partnerships team (ALP) is the face of Spotify to artists, managers, labels and distributors across Sweden. We're looking for a Studio & Project Manager to make our Stockholm studio a place where artists, labels and fans connect, turning the stories behind artists and releases into sessions, video and formats that reach the next generation of listeners. You'll lead the studio and its projects with support from the wider ALP team, and project manage selected ALP initiatives so key partners see Spotify as their number one partner.

    ","id":"6ee8557a-5161-48e6-bba6-c3f8ffe30fda","lists":[{"text":"What You'll Do","content":"

  • Run each studio project from brief to wrap, covering scope, timeline and run-of-show, in partnership with an Audio Engineer and the wider ALP team
  • Manage project budgets for studio support, photographers, licensing and freelancers, and make sure agreements with artists, labels and vendors are in place with a fair value exchange
  • Adapt global video initiatives and formats for Sweden and the Nordics, track results, and evolve the program to fit market needs
  • Partner with Marketing and Growth to promote studio content on the Spotify platform through in-app placements such as banners and Marquee-style campaigns
  • Project manage selected ALP initiatives, such as live events, marketing campaigns and superfan activations, from planning to delivery
  • Build relationships with artists, managers, labels and industry organisations across Sweden, and turn music industry trends and Gen Z discovery habits into new opportunities

    In your role, you will focus on compliance and reporting. Spotify reports indirect taxes in more than 90 countries globally and you will be a key member of the team responsible for ensuring the completeness, timeliness and accuracy of Spotify’s global indirect tax compliance obligations. You will work in close collaboration with global tax team members in both Stockholm and New York, and work cross functionally with various accounting and finance teams.

    We are a team of highly skilled and dedicated colleagues and we offer a challenging and dynamic role in an ever changing environment with the opportunity to take on much responsibility in a rapidly growing international company.   • Prepare indirect tax returns ensuring they are filed timely and accurate.
  • Calculate indirect taxes and ensure timely payments.
  • Analyze data and transactions to ensure correct reporting.
  • Assist with gathering and analyzing data for indirect tax audits and internal audits.
  • Support in monitoring Indirect Tax rules and regulations all over the world.
  • Coordinate with, and support, Finance and Accounting teams as necessary and assist in processes that involve indirect tax.
  • Assist with new tax registrations where needed.
  • Work with external service providers and foreign tax authorities.
  • Participate in process improvement projects
  • Assist in other tax compliance areas such as digital services tax.
  • Other projects as required.

  • University degree with relevant education such as law degree, accounting, CPA, or any combination thereof.
  • Approximately 2 years of relevant tax related work experience.
  • Experience from indirect tax compliance work on a global scale is a big plus.
  • Excellent English skills, both verbally and written. Other language skills are helpful.

Tech.eu https://tech.eu en Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:53:00 +0000 hourly 1 <![CDATA[Jensen Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO following “input” from US government]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-following-input-from-us-government/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-following-input-from-us-government/#comments Jensen Huang has been reinstated as CEO and president of Nvidia, the Nvidia board announced today, in a shock announcement.

The Nvidia board said it had voted unanimously to reinstate Huang, who resigned earlier this month, following reports of extramarital affairs, including with a businesswoman US authorities suspected of spying for China.

Huang admitted he had an affair with the woman who was allleged to be a Chinese spy.

Huang, the Nvidia co-founder, is synonymous with Nvidia, which is the US tech firm powering much of the AI revolution. Hs is returning as leader wiith immediate effect, the board said.

Nvidia said its decision to reinstate Huang came after “input from senior levels of the United States government".

The decision follows President Donald Trump on Sunday night posting on social media: “I hope the Board of Nvidia rehires Jensen Huang. It would be the best thing for the Company, and also, for the USA."

In a statement, the board said: “The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.

"In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk."

“The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia, and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers,” said Harvey C. Jones, Chair of the Board.

“We have every confidence in Jensen and look forward to working with him as he resumes his leadership of the Company. We are grateful to Colette Kress for her outstanding service as interim CEO, in addition to her continuing responsibilities as Nvidia's Chief Financial Officer.” 

President Trump endorsed the decision, saying the board had "made the correct and proper decision".

Image: ChatGPT

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-following-input-from-us-government/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 14:53:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/jensen-huang-reinstated-as-nvidia-ceo-following-input-from-us-government/feed 0 false <![CDATA[BBB invests £43M in Oxford University spinout backer]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/bbb-invests-ps43m-in-oxford-university-spinout-backer/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/bbb-invests-ps43m-in-oxford-university-spinout-backer/#comments The British Business Bank (BBB) has acquired a £43m stake in Oxford Science Enterprises (OSE), an independent venture company that helps turn University of Oxford research into startups.

The £43m investment marks the BBB’s first investment in OSE, as it looks to scale the UK’s university spinout ecosystem.

The UK state-owned BBB and OSE have previously co-invested in ten Oxford University spinouts, most recently AI chip startup Fractile, with OSE the first investor in Fractile. They have also co-invested in OMass Therapeutics, Quantum Motion, and Oxford Quantum Circuits.

European spinouts have raised $13.8bn so far in 2026, with OSE’s portfolio contributing $1.5bn in the first nine months.

The BBB said the partnership between the BBB and the OBE will deepen collaboration on future co-investments and give OSE’s portfolio companies greater access to the BBB’s long-term capital as they scale.

OSE, founded in 2015, is an independent investment company, which aims to turn University of Oxford research into startups. It works with academics to form companies and invests in areas including life sciences, healthtech and deeptech. The University of Oxford owns five per cent of OSE.

OSE has had two major exits behind it: quantum computing company Oxford Ionics was acquired by US-listed IonQ for $1.075bn last year and biotech firm Dark Blue Therapeutics was acquired by Amgen in a $840m deaf completed last year.

Leandros Kalisperas, Chief Investment Officer, the British Business Bank, said: “By working more closely with OSE, we aim to help high-potential spinouts to grow faster and ensure the UK benefits from the breakthroughs it creates.”

Ed Bussey, CEO of Oxford Science Enterprises, said: “OSE is emerging as the world’s largest venture builder of deep science companies dedicated to a single university – a flagship in an area in which the UK now leads the world, at a time of unparalleled need for stronger economic growth and national resilience.

“This investment is a hugely welcome endorsement of the strategic importance of OSE to the UK’s future prosperity, health and security and I’m looking forward to working closely with the British Business Bank to meaningfully improve all of these outcomes to the benefit of the whole of the UK.”

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/bbb-invests-ps43m-in-oxford-university-spinout-backer/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:53:00 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/bbb-invests-ps43m-in-oxford-university-spinout-backer/feed 0 false <![CDATA[Defence startup Agon raises $70M, with UK's SovAI and NSSIF investing]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/defence-startup-agon-raises-70m-with-uk-sovai-and-nssif-investing/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/23/defence-startup-agon-raises-70m-with-uk-sovai-and-nssif-investing/#comments A British defence startup founded by a former Anduril director, which is building virtual battlefields where AI-powered autonomous weapons practice fighting, has raised $70m in a Series A fuding round, less than six months after its $30m seed funding round.

Agon's new funding round was led by existing investor Northzone, along with other existing investors, including Lakestar, XYZ, Lux Capital, Global Founders Capital, and Speedinvest.

The UK Sovereign AI Fund, the UK government's VC fund established to scale up UK AI startups, and the National Security Strategic Investment Fund (NSSIF), the UK government's deeptech venture capital fund for national security and defence, have invested together for the first time, Agon said.

Roelof Botha, who led Sequoia between 2022 and 2025, has also invested.

The latest funding round values Agon at $450m and Agon says it marks one of the largest European defence technology Series A rounds of 2026. In total, it has now raised around $100m.

Founded in 2026, Agon is pitching itself as a startup that builds the infrastructure that designs, trains and iterates AI systems faster than adversaries.  Its tech provides its customers with AI training data to help in combat. The startup is making a play about its sovereign credentials, saying that Europe needs the sovereign capability to train and evolve AI.

It says it has signed initial partnerships with European defence companies and government customers. Its “synthetic” battlefield is aimed at helping its customers train their weapons to repel enemies, so for instance, using AI technology, counterdrone weapons can practice downing drone swarms or test how autonomous systems operate when communications are disrupted, navigation is degraded or adversary tactics change.

It claims that its technology gives defence companies, AI developers and governments the best chance of success on the battlefield.

  • Free choice of registration – Weakened: Founders can choose where to incorporate, but national authorities have more room to challenge that choice in certain circumstances, creating legal uncertainty.

The organisations judge EU Inc by one simple test: Would a founder choose it over a Delaware C-Corp?

The Commission's original proposal passes that test.

The Council's mandate does not.

A call to Member States to change course – and get EU Inc right

The call follows a joint letter to Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, in which both organisations reaffirm their strong support for the Commission's original proposal and call for Member States to reconsider their positions.

For Simon Schaefer, President of Startups for Europe and Co-Initiator EU-INC, the responsibility now lies with Member States to put Europe's collective interests ahead of national compromises:

“A truly European company standard requires Member States to look beyond their national interests. We cannot spend years negotiating one of Europe's most important competitiveness reforms only to end up with another patchwork of national rules.

Private equity firms use these insights to evaluate market size, analyse competitors and test pricing strategies, including understanding how customers might respond to price increases.

Since launching its first research project, LATO has conducted expert interviews across international markets for investment firms including Verdane, Blume Equity and North Island.

The new funding will support the expansion of LATO's engineering, research and sales teams, alongside further product development to enable its AI agents to conduct a broader range of studies independently.

Having initially focused on institutional investors, the company is also exploring applications for consulting firms conducting market research and businesses evaluating demand before entering new markets.

]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/19/lato-secures-47m-to-automate-customer-and-expert-interviews-with-ai/ Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:15:57 +0000 https://tech.eu/2026/11/19/lato-secures-47m-to-automate-customer-and-expert-interviews-with-ai/feed 0 true <![CDATA[Noah raises €800K to help companies unlock their AI potential]]> https://tech.eu/2026/11/19/noah-raises-eur800k-to-help-companies-unlock-their-ai-potential/ https://tech.eu/2026/11/19/noah-raises-eur800k-to-help-companies-unlock-their-ai-potential/#comments Antwerp-based startup Noah, which develops an AI-powered platform to help companies identify and prioritise opportunities for artificial intelligence adoption, has raised €800,000 from a group of business angels. Investors include Rudi Deruytter, former CEO of B-Bank, entrepreneur Ben Schrauwen and Nicolas Debray of Belgium Startup Ecosystem. The financing is supplemented by subsidies and a bank loan.

Founded by Denis Leysen (CEO), César Van Leuffelen (CPO) and Tom De Smedt (CTO), Noah helps businesses assess where AI can deliver value by analysing internal processes, identifying potential use cases and estimating their financial impact.

While companies increasingly recognise the potential of AI, many struggle to identify where to begin or how to measure its benefits. According to Denis Leysen, CEO and co-founder of Noah, traditional approaches such as hiring consultants or assigning internal teams can be costly and time-consuming, creating demand for faster ways to evaluate AI opportunities.

Noah addresses this challenge through an AI interviewer that conducts 20-minute conversations with employees in multiple languages to identify opportunities for automation and process improvements. According to the company, the platform can complete up to 100 interviews within 24 hours, compared with the month a consultant would typically need to conduct 20 interviews.

The information collected is combined with market data to produce a prioritised list of potential AI applications, including initial estimates of time and cost savings. Feedback loops, follow-up interviews and updated market information help keep these assessments current, while a dashboard allows transformation managers to monitor AI initiatives across teams and identify areas requiring adjustments.

Noah aims to develop its platform into a central system for managing digital transformation, expanding beyond identifying AI opportunities to supporting the implementation and monitoring of individual projects.

Every business leader or transformation manager should open Noah first thing on Monday morning, because the agent has kept working on its own over the past week and has new insights waiting. We want to become the standard system for digital transformation,

said César Van Leuffelen, CPO and co-founder of Noah.

The new funding will support further product development and team expansion. The company also plans to expand internationally after 2027.
